value.behaviour: When a docs reader URL's entity does not exist, resolves its ref as a former ref and navigates to the renamed entity's docs URL preserving the docs sub-path, query and fragment.
rules: 1. Export one hook, `useFormerRefRedirect(entityRef: CompoundEntityRef)`, returning `{ shouldShowProgress: boolean }`. Mark it `@internal`: it is not part of the package's public API.

2. Model it directly on the sibling `useExternalRedirect` in this same directory, including its `checkedEntityRef` useRef guard against remount flicker and its `entityKey = stringifyEntityRef(entityRef)` stable dependency. Do not modify useExternalRedirect itself — the two concerns are distinct and must not share one useAsync.

3. Inside a single `useAsync` keyed on `[entityKey, catalogApi]`: first call `catalogApi.getEntityByRef(entityRef)` inside a try/catch. If it returns a truthy entity, return `undefined` — the entity exists, so this hook does nothing and the ordinary docs flow proceeds. This is what keeps genuine 'docs not built' behaviour unchanged: CONTENT_NOT_FOUND for an entity that DOES exist never reaches this code.

4. Only when the entity is absent, call `resolveFormerEntityRef(catalogApi, entityKey)`. On status 'resolved', return the computed target URL plus the former ref; on 'unknown', return `undefined` so the existing behaviour is untouched.
5. Swallow every error from both calls and return `undefined`, exactly as useExternalRedirect does: this is a render path and it must never throw.

6. TARGET URL, preserving the docs sub-path: get `docsRoute = useRouteRef(rootDocsRouteRef)`. Compute `oldBase = docsRoute({ namespace, kind, name })` from the requested ref and `newBase = docsRoute(...)` from the resolved entity's kind, namespace and name, lowercased the way rootDocsRouteRef params are built elsewhere in this plugin. Take `useLocation()`'s pathname; if it starts with `oldBase`, the target is `newBase` plus the remainder after `oldBase`; otherwise `newBase` alone. Append `location.search` and `location.hash` verbatim. This makes a stale /docs/default/component/old-name/some/page land on /docs/default/component/new-name/some/page.

7. In a `useEffect`, when the async value holds a target, call `navigate(target, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef } })` — the same navigation-state carrier the catalog redirect uses, so the one notice component serves both. When the async settles with no target, set `checkedEntityRef.current = entityKey` so a sub-page navigation within the same entity does not re-check.
8. `shouldShowProgress` follows useExternalRedirect's formula: true while checking a not-yet-checked entity, or whenever a target exists and navigation is pending.

9. Import resolveFormerEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-client' (already a dependency of this package), CompoundEntityRef and stringifyEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-model', catalogApiRef from '@backstage/plugin-catalog-react', and rootDocsRouteRef from '../../../routes'.
10. Apache 2.0 header with year 2026.

value.behaviour: Proves the docs redirect fires only for a non-existent entity, preserves the docs sub-path, leaves docs-not-built untouched, and never throws.
rules: 1. Mirror the sibling useExternalRedirect.test.tsx exactly in setup: renderHook with a TestApiProvider wrapper supplying catalogApiRef, plus the jest.mock of react-router-dom's useNavigate and of core-plugin-api's useRouteRef.
2. At most four thorough `it` blocks.

3. Block one, docs-not-built is untouched (FR-18): getEntityByRef returns an existing entity. Assert navigate was never called, queryEntities was never called, and shouldShowProgress settles false — so a CONTENT_NOT_FOUND for a real entity behaves exactly as before.

4. Block two, the redirect and sub-path preservation (FR-17, AC-19): getEntityByRef returns undefined and the former-ref query returns one renamed entity. Drive it from a docs location with a sub-path, a query string and a fragment, and assert navigate was called once with `{ replace: true }`, with state carrying the former ref, and with a target holding the new ref plus the same sub-path, query and fragment.

5. Block three, unknown ref changes nothing: getEntityByRef undefined and the query returning zero items yields no navigate and shouldShowProgress settling false, so the existing docs 404 surfaces as it does today.

6. Block four, guarded and safe: repeated re-renders for the same ref issue the lookup only once (the checkedEntityRef guard), and a getEntityByRef that rejects yields no navigate and no thrown error.
7. Do not add a test id. Apache 2.0 header with year 2026.
